# Local Vedic Astrology Chart Engine (Phase 1)

## Context

The user wants to build a project inspired by [arthiqlabs/vedaksha](https://github.com/arthiqlabs/vedaksha) (a Rust-based Vedic astrology + ephemeris engine with an MCP server for AI agents). Key constraints the user gave, over several rounds of clarification:

- **Local only, no network API calls, ever** — all computation and data must live on disk.
- **Industrial-level code standards** — proper structure, types, tests — even though it's for local/personal use.
- **Python**, using an existing ephemeris library rather than reimplementing orbital mechanics from JPL kernels.
- Chart output in **South Indian style** (fixed 4x4 grid, signs fixed per cell, ascendant marked) — other styles (North/East Indian) offered as config options, not hard-coded.
- No drag-and-drop UI needed — "moving/shifting of signs" turned out to mean configurable chart style / ayanamsha / house system settings, not an interactive UI.
- A single-screen local web UI: one page with a form (birth date/time/place) and the rendered chart, built with **FastAPI + a plain HTML/CSS page** (server-rendered, local only — the browser talks to a server on your own machine, never the internet). No separate CLI.
- MCP server (so Claude/agents can call the chart engine as local tools) should be part of this build, not deferred indefinitely — but built after the core math is solid and tested, since that's the error-prone part.
- Full "kundali essentials" for the first working version: birth chart (D1), houses, nakshatras+pada, Navamsa (D9), Panchanga, Vimshottari Dasha.

This plan covers **Phase 1**: a tested, working core engine + single-screen local web UI. MCP server and deeper features (more vargas, more dasha systems, shadbala, Western astrology, graph layer) are named as Phase 2/3 but not built now.

## Architecture

Four layers, each independently testable:

1. **Ephemeris layer** — wraps `pyswisseph` (Swiss Ephemeris). Given a UTC datetime + lat/lon, returns raw planetary longitudes. Pure astronomy, no astrology concepts yet. Runs fully offline (Swiss Ephemeris supports a built-in analytical "Moshier" mode requiring zero external data files — this is the default so there is never a download step).
2. **Astrology logic layer** — pure Python, converts raw longitudes into Vedic concepts: rashi (sign), bhava (house, whole-sign system), nakshatra + pada, Navamsa (D9), Panchanga (tithi/vara/nakshatra/yoga/karana), Vimshottari Dasha timeline.
3. **Rendering layer** — turns the computed chart into a South Indian-style chart, rendered as an HTML/CSS grid (fixed 4x4 layout minus center) for the browser; North/East Indian and other export formats are later options via a `style` setting.
4. **Interface layer** — a FastAPI app serving **one HTML page**: a form for birth date/time/place, which posts to a local endpoint and re-renders the same page with the chart. Runs at `localhost`, no internet involved. MCP server comes after this, as a thin wrapper exposing the same engine functions as tools.

```
Birth data (date, time, lat/lon, tz)
        │  entered in the browser form, posted to the local FastAPI server
        ▼
 [1] ephemeris.py  ── pyswisseph ──▶ raw planetary longitudes
        │
        ▼
 [2] rashi_bhava.py, nakshatra.py, varga.py, panchanga.py, dasha.py
        │
        ▼
 [3] chart_render.py ──▶ South Indian chart as HTML/CSS grid
        │
        ▼
 [4] web/app.py (FastAPI, Phase 1)  →  mcp_server.py (Phase 2)
```

## Tech stack & why

| Tool | Role | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pyswisseph` | Ephemeris + sidereal/ayanamsha math | Industry-standard for Vedic astrology, offline-capable (Moshier mode needs no data files), has built-in ayanamsha and house-system support. AGPL-licensed — fine for local/personal use; flagged to the user already. |
| `pydantic` v2 | Typed data models (BirthData, PlanetPosition, KundaliChart, etc.) | Validates inputs/outputs, catches mistakes early, self-documenting |
| `fastapi` + `uvicorn` | Local web server | Serves the single-page UI at `localhost`; `uvicorn` is the local server process that runs it — nothing external |
| `jinja2` | HTML templating | Renders the form + chart grid as one server-rendered HTML page |
| `pytest` | Test suite | Regression protection for the astrology math, which is easy to get subtly wrong |
| `pyproject.toml` (hatchling backend) | Packaging | Standard, minimal, no extra tooling required |

Timezone/coordinates: Phase 1 takes **latitude, longitude, and UTC offset (or IANA timezone name) as direct input** rather than a place-name geocoder — avoids pulling in a network-based geocoding service. A local place-name → coordinates lookup (offline gazetteer package) is a Phase 2 convenience addition once the core is proven.

Defaults (all overridable via config/CLI flags): **Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsha**, **whole-sign house system**, **mean node** for Rahu/Ketu, **South Indian** chart style — these are the conventional defaults used by most Indian Panchangs.

## Project layout

```
notes/
  pyproject.toml
  README.md
  src/
    vedic_astro/
      __init__.py
      models.py          # Pydantic models: BirthData, PlanetPosition, HousePlacement, KundaliChart, PanchangaResult, DashaPeriod
      ephemeris.py        # pyswisseph wrapper: raw planetary longitudes for a UTC datetime + location
      rashi_bhava.py       # sign + whole-sign house assignment, ascendant/lagna calculation
      nakshatra.py         # nakshatra + pada lookup from longitude
      varga.py             # divisional charts, starting with Navamsa (D9)
      panchanga.py         # tithi, vara, nakshatra, yoga, karana for a date/place
      dasha.py             # Vimshottari Dasha (starting balance + full sequence, current active period)
      chart_render.py      # South Indian (default) / North / East Indian chart layout logic (HTML-ready structure)
      web/
        app.py             # FastAPI app: GET shows the empty form, POST computes + re-renders with the chart
        templates/
          index.html        # single page: form + chart grid, rendered via Jinja2
        static/
          style.css          # South Indian grid styling
  tests/
    test_ephemeris.py
    test_rashi_bhava.py
    test_nakshatra.py
    test_varga.py
    test_panchanga.py
    test_dasha.py
    test_chart_render.py
    test_web_app.py       # FastAPI TestClient: form submission returns a correctly rendered chart
```

Package name: `vedic_astro` (easy to rename later if the user wants a different project name).

## Build order (each step runs and is checkable before moving on)

1. **`models.py` + `ephemeris.py`** — define the core data shapes, then wrap `pyswisseph` to return raw planetary longitudes (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu) for a given UTC datetime + lat/lon, in sidereal mode with Lahiri ayanamsha.
   - *Verify:* run against a known birth datetime, cross-check planetary degrees against a trusted reference chart (e.g. the user's own known chart from an existing trusted app).
2. **`rashi_bhava.py`** — compute ascendant (lagna), assign each planet a rashi (sign) and bhava (house, whole-sign).
   - *Verify:* same reference chart — signs/houses should match.
3. **`nakshatra.py` + `varga.py` (Navamsa/D9)** — nakshatra + pada per planet, D9 chart placement.
4. **`panchanga.py`** — tithi/vara/nakshatra/yoga/karana for the birth date and location.
5. **`dasha.py`** — Vimshottari Dasha: starting nakshatra-lord balance, full 120-year sequence, current active mahadasha/antardasha as of a given date.
6. **`chart_render.py`** — structure the full computed chart (steps 2-5) into the fixed South Indian grid layout (which sign goes in which of the 12 cells, ascendant marked, planets placed).
7. **`web/app.py` + `templates/index.html`** — FastAPI app with one route: `GET /` shows the birth-data form (date, time, latitude, longitude, UTC offset), `POST /` computes the chart and re-renders the same page with the South Indian grid (HTML/CSS) plus nakshatra/panchanga/dasha info below it. Run locally with `uvicorn` — opens in your browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
8. **Full pytest suite** covering steps 1-7 against the reference chart(s), run at each step rather than only at the end.

Each numbered step gets its own test file and is confirmed working before the next step starts.

## Deferred to later phases (not built now)

- MCP server exposing engine functions as tools (Phase 2, right after Phase 1 is solid).
- Offline place-name → coordinates lookup (Phase 2).
- Additional divisional charts beyond D9, additional dasha systems, shadbala, aspects (graha drishti), Ashtakoot compatibility (Phase 2/3).
- North/East Indian chart rendering, SVG/image output (Phase 2, config already leaves room for this).
- Western astrology, graph/query layer (Phase 3, only if wanted later).

## Verification plan

- `pytest` run after every module lands (not just at the end).
- Cross-check at least one full chart's output (planet signs, houses, nakshatras, Navamsa, current dasha) against a trusted existing Vedic astrology source using the user's own real birth details, since that's the most meaningful correctness check available without a formal test-oracle dataset.
- Web smoke test: run the FastAPI app locally (`uvicorn vedic_astro.web.app:app --reload`), open `http://127.0.0.1:8000` in a browser, submit real birth details on the one-screen form, and confirm the South Indian chart renders correctly with all sections (planets, houses, nakshatras, Navamsa, panchanga, dasha).

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from vedic_astro.web.app import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_get_root_shows_empty_form() -> None:
    response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "Date of birth" in response.text
    assert "Generate chart" in response.text


def test_post_valid_birth_data_renders_chart() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "latitude": "13.0827",
            "longitude": "80.2707",
            "utc_offset_hours": "5.5",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "South Indian chart" in response.text
    assert "Ascendant (Lagna)" in response.text
    assert "Vimshottari Dasha" in response.text


def test_post_invalid_latitude_shows_error() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "latitude": "200",  # out of range
            "longitude": "80.2707",
            "utc_offset_hours": "5.5",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 400
    assert "error" in response.text.lower() or "Generate chart" in response.text


def test_post_unparseable_date_shows_error() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "not-a-date",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "latitude": "13.0827",
            "longitude": "80.2707",
            "utc_offset_hours": "5.5",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 400

"""Thin wrapper around pyswisseph: raw sidereal planetary longitudes only.

No astrology concepts (signs, houses, nakshatras) live here - just "where is
this body, in degrees, right now". Runs fully offline: FLG_MOSEPH selects
Swiss Ephemeris' built-in analytical model, which needs no external data
files (no download, no network call, ever).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime

import swisseph as swe

from vedic_astro.models import NodeType, Planet

_AYANAMSHA_MODES: dict[str, int] = {
    "lahiri": swe.SIDM_LAHIRI,
    "raman": swe.SIDM_RAMAN,
    "krishnamurti": swe.SIDM_KRISHNAMURTI,
}

_SWE_PLANET_IDS: dict[Planet, int] = {
    Planet.SUN: swe.SUN,
    Planet.MOON: swe.MOON,
    Planet.MARS: swe.MARS,
    Planet.MERCURY: swe.MERCURY,
    Planet.JUPITER: swe.JUPITER,
    Planet.VENUS: swe.VENUS,
    Planet.SATURN: swe.SATURN,
}

_CALC_FLAGS = swe.FLG_SIDEREAL | swe.FLG_SPEED | swe.FLG_MOSEPH


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RawPosition:
    """A body's sidereal ecliptic longitude and daily motion, nothing else."""

    longitude: float  # degrees, 0-360
    speed_longitude: float  # degrees/day; negative means retrograde

    @property
    def retrograde(self) -> bool:
        return self.speed_longitude < 0


def julian_day_ut(utc_dt: datetime) -> float:
    hour = utc_dt.hour + utc_dt.minute / 60 + utc_dt.second / 3600
    return swe.julday(utc_dt.year, utc_dt.month, utc_dt.day, hour)


def configure_ayanamsha(ayanamsha: str) -> None:
    mode = _AYANAMSHA_MODES.get(ayanamsha.lower())
    if mode is None:
        known = ", ".join(sorted(_AYANAMSHA_MODES))
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported ayanamsha {ayanamsha!r}; known: {known}")
    swe.set_sid_mode(mode)


def planet_positions(
    utc_dt: datetime, ayanamsha: str, node_type: NodeType
) -> dict[Planet, RawPosition]:
    """Sidereal longitude + speed for all 9 grahas at the given UTC moment."""
    configure_ayanamsha(ayanamsha)
    jd = julian_day_ut(utc_dt)

    positions: dict[Planet, RawPosition] = {}
    for planet, swe_id in _SWE_PLANET_IDS.items():
        values, _flags = swe.calc_ut(jd, swe_id, _CALC_FLAGS)
        lon, _lat, _dist, lon_speed, _lat_speed, _dist_speed = values
        positions[planet] = RawPosition(longitude=lon % 360, speed_longitude=lon_speed)

    node_id = swe.MEAN_NODE if node_type == NodeType.MEAN else swe.TRUE_NODE
    node_values, _flags = swe.calc_ut(jd, node_id, _CALC_FLAGS)
    rahu_lon, _lat, _dist, rahu_speed, _lat_speed, _dist_speed = node_values
    positions[Planet.RAHU] = RawPosition(longitude=rahu_lon % 360, speed_longitude=rahu_speed)
    # Ketu is always exactly opposite Rahu - not an independent body in Swiss Ephemeris.
    positions[Planet.KETU] = RawPosition(
        longitude=(rahu_lon + 180) % 360, speed_longitude=rahu_speed
    )

    return positions


def ascendant_longitude(
    utc_dt: datetime, latitude: float, longitude: float, ayanamsha: str
) -> float:
    """Sidereal longitude of the ascendant (lagna), 0-360 degrees."""
    configure_ayanamsha(ayanamsha)
    jd = julian_day_ut(utc_dt)
    _cusps, ascmc = swe.houses_ex(jd, latitude, longitude, b"W", swe.FLG_SIDEREAL)
    return ascmc[0] % 360

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache()
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlaceMatch:
    name: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:
    countries = _cache.get_countries()
    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))


def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:
    """Find candidate cities for free-text like "Chennai" or "Chennai, India".

    Returns the largest-population, most-exact matches first. Empty if the
    query is blank or matches nothing.
    """
    query = query.strip()
    if not query:
        return []

    if "," in query:
        city_part, country_part = (part.strip() for part in query.split(",", 1))
    else:
        city_part, country_part = query, ""
    city_lower = city_part.lower()
    country_lower = country_part.lower()

    def matches_country(city: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
        if not country_lower:
            return True
        code = str(city["countrycode"]).lower()
        return country_lower == code or country_lower in _country_name(str(city["countrycode"])).lower()

    cities = _cache.get_cities()
    candidates = [
        city for city in cities.values()
        if city_lower in str(city["name"]).lower() and matches_country(city)
    ]
    if not candidates:
        # Fall back to alternate names/spellings (e.g. "Madras" for Chennai).
        candidates = [
            city for city in cities.values()
            if matches_country(city)
            and any(city_lower == str(alt).lower() for alt in city.get("alternatenames", []))
        ]

    candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (str(c["name"]).lower() != city_lower, -int(c["population"])))  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    return [
        PlaceMatch(
            name=str(city["name"]),
            country=_country_name(str(city["countrycode"])),
            latitude=float(city["latitude"]),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            longitude=float(city["longitude"]),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            timezone=str(city["timezone"]),
        )
        for city in candidates[:limit]
    ]


def resolve_utc_offset(
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    local_date: date,
    local_time: time,
    timezone_name: str | None = None,
) -> float:
    """UTC offset in effect at this place on this specific date (accounts for
    historical DST rules) - derived from local IANA tzdata, not a network call.
    """
    tz_name = timezone_name or _timezone_finder.timezone_at(lat=latitude, lng=longitude)
    if tz_name is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a timezone for coordinates ({latitude}, {longitude})")
    zone = ZoneInfo(tz_name)
    aware_local = datetime.combine(local_date, local_time, tzinfo=zone)
    offset = aware_local.utcoffset()
    if offset is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a UTC offset for timezone {tz_name!r}")
    return offset.total_seconds() / 3600

from datetime import date, time

import pytest

from vedic_astro.geocode import resolve_utc_offset, search_places


def test_search_finds_chennai() -> None:
    results = search_places("Chennai")
    assert any(r.name == "Chennai" and r.country == "India" for r in results)


def test_search_by_alternate_name_madras() -> None:
    results = search_places("Madras")
    assert any(r.name == "Chennai" for r in results)


def test_search_with_country_filter() -> None:
    results = search_places("Chennai, India")
    assert all(r.country == "India" for r in results)
    assert len(results) >= 1


def test_search_empty_query_returns_nothing() -> None:
    assert search_places("") == []
    assert search_places("   ") == []


def test_search_nonexistent_place_returns_nothing() -> None:
    assert search_places("Zzzznotarealplacexyz123") == []


def test_search_ambiguous_name_returns_multiple() -> None:
    # "Springfield" exists in several US states - a classic disambiguation case.
    results = search_places("Springfield")
    assert len(results) > 1


def test_resolve_utc_offset_chennai_matches_known_ist() -> None:
    # India Standard Time is a fixed UTC+5:30 year-round (no DST).
    offset = resolve_utc_offset(13.0827, 80.2707, date(1990, 6, 15), time(8, 30), "Asia/Kolkata")
    assert offset == pytest.approx(5.5)


def test_resolve_utc_offset_without_timezone_name_uses_coordinates() -> None:
    offset = resolve_utc_offset(13.0827, 80.2707, date(1990, 6, 15), time(8, 30))
    assert offset == pytest.approx(5.5)


def test_resolve_utc_offset_accounts_for_dst() -> None:
    # New York: EST (UTC-5) in January, EDT (UTC-4) in July.
    winter_offset = resolve_utc_offset(40.7128, -74.0060, date(2024, 1, 15), time(12, 0), "America/New_York")
    summer_offset = resolve_utc_offset(40.7128, -74.0060, date(2024, 7, 15), time(12, 0), "America/New_York")
    assert winter_offset == pytest.approx(-5.0)
    assert summer_offset == pytest.approx(-4.0)

input.content:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from vedic_astro.web.app import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_get_root_shows_empty_form() -> None:
    response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "Place of birth" in response.text
    assert "Generate chart" in response.text


def test_post_with_place_name_renders_chart() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "place_name": "Chennai, India",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "South Indian chart" in response.text
    assert "Ascendant (Lagna)" in response.text
    assert "Vimshottari Dasha" in response.text
    assert "Chennai" in response.text


def test_post_with_manual_coordinates_renders_chart() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "manual_latitude": "13.0827",
            "manual_longitude": "80.2707",
            "manual_utc_offset_hours": "5.5",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "South Indian chart" in response.text


def test_post_ambiguous_place_shows_candidates() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "place_name": "Springfield",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "Which place did you mean" in response.text
    assert "South Indian chart" not in response.text


def test_post_unknown_place_shows_error() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "place_name": "Zzzznotarealplacexyz123",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 400
    assert "No place found" in response.text


def test_post_no_place_or_coordinates_shows_error() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 400


def test_post_invalid_manual_latitude_shows_error() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "manual_latitude": "200",  # out of range
            "manual_longitude": "80.2707",
            "manual_utc_offset_hours": "5.5",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 400


def test_post_unparseable_date_shows_error() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "not-a-date",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "place_name": "Chennai, India",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 400


def test_post_selected_candidate_renders_chart() -> None:
    response = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "birth_date": "1990-06-15",
            "birth_time": "08:30:00",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
            "selected_latitude": "13.08784",
            "selected_longitude": "80.27847",
            "selected_timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
            "selected_label": "Chennai, India",
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "South Indian chart" in response.text
    assert "Chennai, India" in response.text

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache()
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlaceMatch:
    name: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:
    countries = _cache.get_countries()
    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))


def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:
    """Find candidate cities for free-text like "Chennai" or "Chennai, India".

    Returns the largest-population, most-exact matches first. Empty if the
    query is blank or matches nothing.
    """
    query = query.strip()
    if not query:
        return []

    if "," in query:
        city_part, country_part = (part.strip() for part in query.split(",", 1))
    else:
        city_part, country_part = query, ""
    city_lower = city_part.lower()
    country_lower = country_part.lower()

    def matches_country(city: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
        if not country_lower:
            return True
        code = str(city["countrycode"]).lower()
        return country_lower == code or country_lower in _country_name(str(city["countrycode"])).lower()

    cities = _cache.get_cities()
    candidates = [
        city for city in cities.values()
        if city_lower in str(city["name"]).lower() and matches_country(city)
    ]
    if not candidates:
        # Fall back to alternate names/spellings (e.g. "Madras" for Chennai).
        candidates = [
            city for city in cities.values()
            if matches_country(city)
            and any(city_lower == str(alt).lower() for alt in city.get("alternatenames", []))
        ]

    candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (str(c["name"]).lower() != city_lower, -int(c["population"])))  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    return [
        PlaceMatch(
            name=str(city["name"]),
            country=_country_name(str(city["countrycode"])),
            latitude=float(city["latitude"]),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            longitude=float(city["longitude"]),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            timezone=str(city["timezone"]),
        )
        for city in candidates[:limit]
    ]


def resolve_utc_offset(
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    local_date: date,
    local_time: time,
    timezone_name: str | None = None,
) -> float:
    """UTC offset in effect at this place on this specific date (accounts for
    historical DST rules) - derived from local IANA tzdata, not a network call.
    """
    tz_name = timezone_name or _timezone_finder.timezone_at(lat=latitude, lng=longitude)
    if tz_name is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a timezone for coordinates ({latitude}, {longitude})")
    zone = ZoneInfo(tz_name)
    aware_local = datetime.combine(local_date, local_time, tzinfo=zone)
    offset = aware_local.utcoffset()
    if offset is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a UTC offset for timezone {tz_name!r}")
    return offset.total_seconds() / 3600

**Ayanamsha**: a technical correction number used to convert Western zodiac positions into the Vedic (sidereal) zodiac. """Single-screen local web UI: one form, one rendered South Indian chart.

Runs entirely on localhost via uvicorn - the browser only ever talks to this
process on your own machine, never the internet. Place-of-birth lookup and
timezone resolution are both offline (see geocode.py) - only exact
coordinates under "Advanced" bypass them entirely.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
from pydantic import ValidationError

from vedic_astro.chart import build_kundali_chart
from vedic_astro.chart_render import south_indian_layout
from vedic_astro.geocode import resolve_utc_offset, search_places
from vedic_astro.models import BirthData, KundaliChart, NodeType

_BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

app = FastAPI(title="vedic-astro")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=_BASE_DIR / "static"), name="static")
templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=_BASE_DIR / "templates")

_AYANAMSHA_CHOICES = ["lahiri", "raman", "krishnamurti"]


def _current_local_datetime(utc_offset_hours: float) -> datetime:
    """'Now', expressed as a naive datetime in the birth place's local time -
    consistent with the naive local datetimes used throughout the dasha math."""
    now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
    return now_utc + timedelta(hours=utc_offset_hours)


def _empty_form_context() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "ayanamsha_choices": _AYANAMSHA_CHOICES,
        "form_values": {
            "birth_date": "",
            "birth_time": "",
            "place_name": "",
            "manual_latitude": "",
            "manual_longitude": "",
            "manual_utc_offset_hours": "",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
        "chart": None,
        "grid": None,
        "current_mahadasha": None,
        "current_antardasha": None,
        "resolved_place": None,
        "candidates": None,
        "error": None,
    }


def _render(request: Request, context: dict[str, object], status_code: int = 200) -> HTMLResponse:
    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, "index.html", context, status_code=status_code)


@app.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def show_form(request: Request) -> HTMLResponse:
    return _render(request, _empty_form_context())


@app.post("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def compute_chart(
    request: Request,
    birth_date: str = Form(...),
    birth_time: str = Form(...),
    place_name: str = Form(""),
    manual_latitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_longitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_utc_offset_hours: str = Form(""),
    selected_latitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_longitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_timezone: str = Form(""),
    selected_label: str = Form(""),
    ayanamsha: str = Form("lahiri"),
    node_type: str = Form("mean"),
) -> HTMLResponse:
    context = _empty_form_context()
    context["form_values"] = {
        "birth_date": birth_date,
        "birth_time": birth_time,
        "place_name": place_name,
        "manual_latitude": manual_latitude,
        "manual_longitude": manual_longitude,
        "manual_utc_offset_hours": manual_utc_offset_hours,
        "ayanamsha": ayanamsha,
        "node_type": node_type,
    }

    try:
        parsed_date = date.fromisoformat(birth_date)
        parsed_time = time.fromisoformat(birth_time)
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = f"Invalid date or time: {exc}"
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    latitude: float | None = None
    longitude: float | None = None
    resolved_timezone: str | None = None
    resolved_place_label: str | None = None

    if selected_latitude and selected_longitude:
        # User clicked a candidate from the disambiguation list below.
        latitude = float(selected_latitude)
        longitude = float(selected_longitude)
        resolved_timezone = selected_timezone or None
        resolved_place_label = selected_label or None
    elif manual_latitude.strip() and manual_longitude.strip():
        try:
            latitude = float(manual_latitude)
            longitude = float(manual_longitude)
        except ValueError:
            context["error"] = "Latitude/longitude must be numbers."
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
    elif place_name.strip():
        matches = search_places(place_name)
        if not matches:
            context["error"] = (
                f'No place found matching "{place_name}". Try a nearby larger city, '
                "or enter exact coordinates under Advanced below."
            )
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
        if len(matches) > 1:
            context["candidates"] = matches
            return _render(request, context)
        latitude, longitude, resolved_timezone = (
            matches[0].latitude,
            matches[0].longitude,
            matches[0].timezone,
        )
        resolved_place_label = f"{matches[0].name}, {matches[0].country}"
    else:
        context["error"] = "Enter a place of birth, or exact coordinates under Advanced."
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        if manual_utc_offset_hours.strip():
            utc_offset = float(manual_utc_offset_hours)
        else:
            utc_offset = resolve_utc_offset(
                latitude, longitude, parsed_date, parsed_time, resolved_timezone
            )
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = str(exc)
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        birth_data = BirthData(
            birth_date=parsed_date,
            birth_time=parsed_time,
            latitude=latitude,
            longitude=longitude,
            utc_offset_hours=utc_offset,
            ayanamsha=ayanamsha,
            node_type=NodeType(node_type),
        )
        chart: KundaliChart = build_kundali_chart(birth_data)
    except (ValueError, ValidationError) as exc:
        context["error"] = str(exc)
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    now_local = _current_local_datetime(utc_offset)
    context["chart"] = chart
    context["grid"] = south_indian_layout(chart)
    context["current_mahadasha"] = chart.dasha.current_mahadasha(now_local)
    context["current_antardasha"] = chart.dasha.current_antardasha(now_local)
    context["resolved_place"] = resolved_place_label
    return _render(request, context)

process on your own machine, never the internet. Place-of-birth lookup and

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
from pydantic import ValidationError

from vedic_astro.chart import build_kundali_chart
from vedic_astro.chart_render import south_indian_layout
from vedic_astro.geocode import resolve_utc_offset, search_places
from vedic_astro.models import BirthData, KundaliChart, NodeType

_BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

app = FastAPI(title="vedic-astro")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=_BASE_DIR / "static"), name="static")
templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=_BASE_DIR / "templates")

_AYANAMSHA_CHOICES = ["lahiri", "raman", "krishnamurti"]


def _current_local_datetime(utc_offset_hours: float) -> datetime:
    """'Now', expressed as a naive datetime in the birth place's local time -
    consistent with the naive local datetimes used throughout the dasha math."""
    now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
    return now_utc + timedelta(hours=utc_offset_hours)


def _empty_form_context() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "ayanamsha_choices": _AYANAMSHA_CHOICES,
        "form_values": {
            "birth_date": "",

    }

@app.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)

@app.post("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def compute_chart(
    request: Request,
    birth_date: str = Form(...),
    birth_time: str = Form(...),
    place_name: str = Form(""),
    manual_latitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_longitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_utc_offset_hours: str = Form(""),
    selected_latitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_longitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_timezone: str = Form(""),
    selected_label: str = Form(""),
    ayanamsha: str = Form("lahiri"),
    node_type: str = Form("mean"),
) -> HTMLResponse:
    context = _empty_form_context()
    context["form_values"] = {
        "birth_date": birth_date,
        "birth_time": birth_time,
        "place_name": place_name,
        "manual_latitude": manual_latitude,
        "manual_longitude": manual_longitude,
        "manual_utc_offset_hours": manual_utc_offset_hours,
        "ayanamsha": ayanamsha,
        "node_type": node_type,
    }

    try:
        parsed_date = date.fromisoformat(birth_date)
        parsed_time = time.fromisoformat(birth_time)
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = f"Invalid date or time: {exc}"
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    latitude: float | None = None
    longitude: float | None = None
    resolved_timezone: str | None = None
    resolved_place_label: str | None = None

    if selected_latitude and selected_longitude:
        # User clicked a candidate from the disambiguation list below.
        latitude = float(selected_latitude)
        longitude = float(selected_longitude)
        resolved_timezone = selected_timezone or None
        resolved_place_label = selected_label or None
    elif manual_latitude.strip() and manual_longitude.strip():
        try:
            latitude = float(manual_latitude)
            longitude = float(manual_longitude)
        except ValueError:
            context["error"] = "Latitude/longitude must be numbers."
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
    elif place_name.strip():
        matches = search_places(place_name)
        if not matches:
            context["error"] = (
                f'No place found matching "{place_name}". Try a nearby larger city, '
                "or enter exact coordinates under Advanced below."
            )
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
        if len(matches) > 1:
            context["candidates"] = matches
            return _render(request, context)
        latitude, longitude, resolved_timezone = (
            matches[0].latitude,
            matches[0].longitude,
            matches[0].timezone,
        )
        resolved_place_label = f"{matches[0].name}, {matches[0].country}"
    else:
        context["error"] = "Enter a place of birth, or exact coordinates under Advanced."
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        if manual_utc_offset_hours.strip():
            utc_offset = float(manual_utc_offset_hours)
        else:
            utc_offset = resolve_utc_offset(
                latitude, longitude, parsed_date, parsed_time, resolved_timezone
            )
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = str(exc)
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        birth_data = BirthData(
            birth_date=parsed_date,
            birth_time=parsed_time,
            latitude=latitude,
            longitude=longitude,
            utc_offset_hours=utc_offset,
            ayanamsha=ayanamsha,
            node_type=NodeType(node_type),
        )
        chart: KundaliChart = build_kundali_chart(birth_data)
    except (ValueError, ValidationError) as exc:
        context["error"] = str(exc)
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    now_local = _current_local_datetime(utc_offset)
    context["chart"] = chart
    context["grid"] = south_indian_layout(chart)
    context["current_mahadasha"] = chart.dasha.current_mahadasha(now_local)
    context["current_antardasha"] = chart.dasha.current_antardasha(now_local)
    context["resolved_place"] = resolved_place_label
    return _render(request, context)

33	    countries = _cache.get_countries()
34	    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))

37	def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:
38	    """Find candidate cities for free-text like "Chennai" or "Chennai, India".
39	
40	    Returns the largest-population, most-exact matches first. Empty if the
41	    query is blank or matches nothing.
42	    """
43	    query = query.strip()
44	    if not query:
45	        return []
46	
47	    if "," in query:
48	        city_part, country_part = (part.strip() for part in query.split(",", 1))
49	    else:
50	        city_part, country_part = query, ""
51	    city_lower = city_part.lower()
52	    country_lower = country_part.lower()
53	
54	    def matches_country(city: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
55	        if not country_lower:
56	            return True
57	        code = str(city["countrycode"]).lower()
58	        return country_lower == code or country_lower in _country_name(str(city["countrycode"])).lower()
59	
60	    cities = _cache.get_cities()
61	    candidates = [
62	        city for city in cities.values()
63	        if city_lower in str(city["name"]).lower() and matches_country(city)
64	    ]
65	    if not candidates:
66	        # Fall back to alternate names/spellings (e.g. "Madras" for Chennai).
67	        candidates = [
68	            city for city in cities.values()
69	            if matches_country(city)
70	            and any(city_lower == str(alt).lower() for alt in city.get("alternatenames", []))
71	        ]
72	
73	    candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (str(c["name"]).lower() != city_lower, -int(c["population"])))
74	
75	    return [

77	            name=str(city["name"]),
78	            country=_country_name(str(city["countrycode"])),
79	            latitude=float(city["latitude"]),
80	            longitude=float(city["longitude"]),
81	            timezone=str(city["timezone"]),
82	        )
83	        for city in candidates[:limit]
84	    ]

88	    latitude: float,

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache()
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlaceMatch:
    name: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:
    countries = _cache.get_countries()
    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))


def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:
    """Find candidate cities for free-text like "Chennai" or "Chennai, India".

    Returns the largest-population, most-exact matches first. Empty if the
    query is blank or matches nothing.

    return [
        PlaceMatch(
            name=str(city["name"]),
            country=_country_name(str(city["countrycode"])),
            latitude=float(city["latitude"]),
            longitude=float(city["longitude"]),

        for city in candidates[:limit]
    ]


def resolve_utc_offset(
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,

"""Single-screen local web UI: one form, one rendered South Indian chart.

Runs entirely on localhost via uvicorn - the browser only ever talks to this
process on your own machine, never the internet. Place-of-birth lookup and
timezone resolution are both offline (see geocode.py) - only exact
coordinates under "Advanced" bypass them entirely.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
from pydantic import ValidationError

from vedic_astro.chart import build_kundali_chart
from vedic_astro.chart_render import south_indian_layout
from vedic_astro.geocode import resolve_utc_offset, search_places
from vedic_astro.models import BirthData, KundaliChart, NodeType

_BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

app = FastAPI(title="vedic-astro")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=_BASE_DIR / "static"), name="static")
templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=_BASE_DIR / "templates")

_AYANAMSHA_CHOICES = ["lahiri", "raman", "krishnamurti"]


def _current_local_datetime(utc_offset_hours: float) -> datetime:
    """'Now', expressed as a naive datetime in the birth place's local time -
    consistent with the naive local datetimes used throughout the dasha math."""
    now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
    return now_utc + timedelta(hours=utc_offset_hours)


def _to_24_hour_time(hour_12: int, minute: int, meridiem: str) -> time:
    if not (1 <= hour_12 <= 12):
        raise ValueError("Hour must be between 1 and 12.")
    if not (0 <= minute <= 59):
        raise ValueError("Minute must be between 0 and 59.")
    meridiem = meridiem.upper()
    if meridiem not in ("AM", "PM"):
        raise ValueError("Choose AM or PM.")
    hour_24 = (hour_12 % 12) + (12 if meridiem == "PM" else 0)
    return time(hour_24, minute)


def _empty_form_context() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "ayanamsha_choices": _AYANAMSHA_CHOICES,
        "form_values": {
            "birth_date": "",
            "birth_hour": "",
            "birth_minute": "",
            "birth_meridiem": "AM",
            "place_name": "",
            "manual_latitude": "",
            "manual_longitude": "",
            "manual_utc_offset_hours": "",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
        "chart": None,
        "grid": None,
        "current_mahadasha": None,
        "current_antardasha": None,
        "resolved_place": None,
        "candidates": None,
        "error": None,
    }


def _render(request: Request, context: dict[str, object], status_code: int = 200) -> HTMLResponse:
    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, "index.html", context, status_code=status_code)


@app.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def show_form(request: Request) -> HTMLResponse:
    return _render(request, _empty_form_context())


@app.post("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def compute_chart(
    request: Request,
    birth_date: str = Form(...),
    birth_hour: str = Form(...),
    birth_minute: str = Form(...),
    birth_meridiem: str = Form("AM"),
    place_name: str = Form(""),
    manual_latitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_longitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_utc_offset_hours: str = Form(""),
    selected_latitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_longitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_timezone: str = Form(""),
    selected_label: str = Form(""),
    ayanamsha: str = Form("lahiri"),
    node_type: str = Form("mean"),
) -> HTMLResponse:
    context = _empty_form_context()
    context["form_values"] = {
        "birth_date": birth_date,
        "birth_hour": birth_hour,
        "birth_minute": birth_minute,
        "birth_meridiem": birth_meridiem,
        "place_name": place_name,
        "manual_latitude": manual_latitude,
        "manual_longitude": manual_longitude,
        "manual_utc_offset_hours": manual_utc_offset_hours,
        "ayanamsha": ayanamsha,
        "node_type": node_type,
    }

    try:
        parsed_date = date.fromisoformat(birth_date)
        parsed_time = _to_24_hour_time(int(birth_hour), int(birth_minute), birth_meridiem)
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = f"Invalid date or time: {exc}"
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    latitude: float | None = None
    longitude: float | None = None
    resolved_timezone: str | None = None
    resolved_place_label: str | None = None

    if selected_latitude and selected_longitude:
        # User clicked a candidate from the disambiguation list below.
        latitude = float(selected_latitude)
        longitude = float(selected_longitude)
        resolved_timezone = selected_timezone or None
        resolved_place_label = selected_label or None
    elif manual_latitude.strip() and manual_longitude.strip():
        try:
            latitude = float(manual_latitude)
            longitude = float(manual_longitude)
        except ValueError:
            context["error"] = "Latitude/longitude must be numbers."
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
    elif place_name.strip():
        matches = search_places(place_name)
        if not matches:
            context["error"] = (
                f'No place found matching "{place_name}". Try a nearby larger city, '
                "or enter exact coordinates under Advanced below."
            )
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
        if len(matches) > 1:
            context["candidates"] = matches
            return _render(request, context)
        latitude, longitude, resolved_timezone = (
            matches[0].latitude,
            matches[0].longitude,
            matches[0].timezone,
        )
        resolved_place_label = f"{matches[0].name}, {matches[0].country}"
    else:
        context["error"] = "Enter a place of birth, or exact coordinates under Advanced."
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        if manual_utc_offset_hours.strip():
            utc_offset = float(manual_utc_offset_hours)
        else:
            utc_offset = resolve_utc_offset(
                latitude, longitude, parsed_date, parsed_time, resolved_timezone
            )
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = str(exc)
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        birth_data = BirthData(
            birth_date=parsed_date,
            birth_time=parsed_time,
            latitude=latitude,
            longitude=longitude,
            utc_offset_hours=utc_offset,
            ayanamsha=ayanamsha,
            node_type=NodeType(node_type),
        )
        chart: KundaliChart = build_kundali_chart(birth_data)
    except (ValueError, ValidationError) as exc:
        context["error"] = str(exc)
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    now_local = _current_local_datetime(utc_offset)
    context["chart"] = chart
    context["grid"] = south_indian_layout(chart)
    context["current_mahadasha"] = chart.dasha.current_mahadasha(now_local)
    context["current_antardasha"] = chart.dasha.current_antardasha(now_local)
    context["resolved_place"] = resolved_place_label
    return _render(request, context)

from datetime import date, time

import pytest

from vedic_astro.geocode import resolve_utc_offset, search_places


def test_search_finds_chennai() -> None:
    results = search_places("Chennai")
    assert any(r.name == "Chennai" and r.country == "India" for r in results)


def test_search_by_alternate_name_madras() -> None:
    results = search_places("Madras")
    assert any(r.name == "Chennai" for r in results)


def test_search_with_country_filter() -> None:
    results = search_places("Chennai, India")
    assert all(r.country == "India" for r in results)
    assert len(results) >= 1


def test_search_empty_query_returns_nothing() -> None:
    assert search_places("") == []
    assert search_places("   ") == []


def test_search_nonexistent_place_returns_nothing() -> None:
    assert search_places("Zzzznotarealplacexyz123") == []


def test_search_ambiguous_name_returns_multiple() -> None:
    # "Springfield" exists in several US states - a classic disambiguation case.
    results = search_places("Springfield")
    assert len(results) > 1


def test_resolve_utc_offset_chennai_matches_known_ist() -> None:
    # India Standard Time is a fixed UTC+5:30 year-round (no DST).
    offset = resolve_utc_offset(13.0827, 80.2707, date(1990, 6, 15), time(8, 30), "Asia/Kolkata")
    assert offset == pytest.approx(5.5)


def test_resolve_utc_offset_without_timezone_name_uses_coordinates() -> None:
    offset = resolve_utc_offset(13.0827, 80.2707, date(1990, 6, 15), time(8, 30))
    assert offset == pytest.approx(5.5)


def test_resolve_utc_offset_accounts_for_dst() -> None:
    # New York: EST (UTC-5) in January, EDT (UTC-4) in July.
    winter_offset = resolve_utc_offset(40.7128, -74.0060, date(2024, 1, 15), time(12, 0), "America/New_York")
    summer_offset = resolve_utc_offset(40.7128, -74.0060, date(2024, 7, 15), time(12, 0), "America/New_York")
    assert winter_offset == pytest.approx(-5.0)
    assert summer_offset == pytest.approx(-4.0)

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name. `reverse_geocoder`
adds the state/region name (e.g. "Tamil Nadu", "Illinois") for any country,
also from a dataset bundled inside the package - this is what lets same-named
cities in different states/provinces be told apart during disambiguation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
import reverse_geocoder
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache()
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlaceMatch:
    name: str
    state: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:
    countries = _cache.get_countries()
    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))


def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:
    """Find candidate cities for free-text like "Chennai" or "Chennai, India".

    Returns the largest-population, most-exact matches first. Empty if the
    query is blank or matches nothing.
    """
    query = query.strip()
    if not query:
        return []

    if "," in query:
        city_part, country_part = (part.strip() for part in query.split(",", 1))
    else:
        city_part, country_part = query, ""
    city_lower = city_part.lower()
    country_lower = country_part.lower()

    def matches_country(city: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
        if not country_lower:
            return True
        code = str(city["countrycode"]).lower()
        return country_lower == code or country_lower in _country_name(str(city["countrycode"])).lower()

    cities = _cache.get_cities()
    candidates = [
        city for city in cities.values()
        if city_lower in str(city["name"]).lower() and matches_country(city)
    ]
    if not candidates:
        # Fall back to alternate names/spellings (e.g. "Madras" for Chennai).
        candidates = [
            city for city in cities.values()
            if matches_country(city)
            and any(city_lower == str(alt).lower() for alt in city.get("alternatenames", []))
        ]

    candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (str(c["name"]).lower() != city_lower, -int(c["population"])))
    candidates = candidates[:limit]
    if not candidates:
        return []

    coords = [(float(city["latitude"]), float(city["longitude"])) for city in candidates]
    # mode=1 (single-process, in-memory) - safer than the default multiprocessing
    # mode when called from inside a running web server, and plenty fast for
    # the handful of candidates a disambiguation search ever needs.
    states = reverse_geocoder.search(coords, mode=1, verbose=False)

    return [
        PlaceMatch(
            name=str(city["name"]),
            state=str(state["admin1"]),
            country=_country_name(str(city["countrycode"])),
            latitude=float(city["latitude"]),
            longitude=float(city["longitude"]),
            timezone=str(city["timezone"]),
        )
        for city, state in zip(candidates, states)
    ]


def resolve_utc_offset(
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    local_date: date,
    local_time: time,
    timezone_name: str | None = None,
) -> float:
    """UTC offset in effect at this place on this specific date (accounts for
    historical DST rules) - derived from local IANA tzdata, not a network call.
    """
    tz_name = timezone_name or _timezone_finder.timezone_at(lat=latitude, lng=longitude)
    if tz_name is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a timezone for coordinates ({latitude}, {longitude})")
    zone = ZoneInfo(tz_name)
    aware_local = datetime.combine(local_date, local_time, tzinfo=zone)
    offset = aware_local.utcoffset()
    if offset is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a UTC offset for timezone {tz_name!r}")
    return offset.total_seconds() / 3600

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name. `reverse_geocoder`
adds the state/region name (e.g. "Tamil Nadu", "Illinois") for any country,
also from a dataset bundled inside the package - this is what lets same-named
cities in different states/provinces be told apart during disambiguation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
import reverse_geocoder
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

# min_city_population=500 selects geonamescache's most granular bundled
# dataset (~235,000 places instead of the ~34,000-place default cutoff of
# 15,000) so small towns and villages are findable, not just major cities.
_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache(min_city_population=500)
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlaceMatch:
    name: str
    state: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:
    countries = _cache.get_countries()
    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))


def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:
    """Find candidate cities for free-text like "Chennai" or "Chennai, India".

    Returns the largest-population, most-exact matches first. Empty if the
    query is blank or matches nothing.
    """
    query = query.strip()
    if not query:
        return []

    if "," in query:
        city_part, country_part = (part.strip() for part in query.split(",", 1))
    else:
        city_part, country_part = query, ""
    city_lower = city_part.lower()
    country_lower = country_part.lower()

    def matches_country(city: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
        if not country_lower:
            return True
        code = str(city["countrycode"]).lower()
        return country_lower == code or country_lower in _country_name(str(city["countrycode"])).lower()

    cities = _cache.get_cities()
    candidates = [
        city for city in cities.values()
        if city_lower in str(city["name"]).lower() and matches_country(city)

    if not candidates:

    candidates = candidates[:limit]
    if not candidates:
        return []

    coords = [(float(city["latitude"]), float(city["longitude"])) for city in candidates]
    # mode=1 (single-process, in-memory) - safer than the default multiprocessing
    # mode when called from inside a running web server, and plenty fast for
    # the handful of candidates a disambiguation search ever needs.
    states = reverse_geocoder.search(coords, mode=1, verbose=False)

            name=str(city["name"]),
            state=str(state["admin1"]),
            country=_country_name(str(city["countrycode"])),
            latitude=float(city["latitude"]),
            longitude=float(city["longitude"]),
            timezone=str(city["timezone"]),
        )
        for city, state in zip(candidates, states)
    ]

    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    local_date: date,
    local_time: time,
    timezone_name: str | None = None,
) -> float:
    """UTC offset in effect at this place on this specific date (accounts for
    historical DST rules) - derived from local IANA tzdata, not a network call.

    tz_name = timezone_name or _timezone_finder.timezone_at(lat=latitude, lng=longitude)

    offset = aware_local.utcoffset()
    if offset is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a UTC offset for timezone {tz_name!r}")
    return offset.total_seconds() / 3600

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name. `reverse_geocoder`
adds the state/region name (e.g. "Tamil Nadu", "Illinois") for any country,
also from a dataset bundled inside the package - this is what lets same-named
cities in different states/provinces be told apart during disambiguation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
import reverse_geocoder
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

# min_city_population=500 selects geonamescache's most granular bundled
# dataset (~235,000 places instead of the ~34,000-place default cutoff of
# 15,000) so small towns and villages are findable, not just major cities.
_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache(min_city_population=500)
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()

# Precomputed once at import time, not per search: with ~235,000 places and
# some carrying dozens of alternate spellings, scanning every alternate name
# of every city on every query was measured at ~1.6s/search - too slow for an
# interactive form. An index built once (a few hundred ms) makes each search
# a fast dict lookup instead of a linear scan.
_ALL_CITIES: list[dict[str, object]] = list(_cache.get_cities().values())
_CITIES_WITH_LOWER_NAME: list[tuple[dict[str, object], str]] = [
    (city, str(city["name"]).lower()) for city in _ALL_CITIES
]
_ALTERNATE_NAME_INDEX: dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]] = {}
for _city in _ALL_CITIES:
    for _alt in _city.get("alternatenames", []):  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        _ALTERNATE_NAME_INDEX.setdefault(str(_alt).lower(), []).append(_city)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlaceMatch:
    name: str
    state: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:
    countries = _cache.get_countries()
    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))


def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:
    """Find candidate cities for free-text like "Chennai" or "Chennai, India".

    Returns the largest-population, most-exact matches first. Empty if the
    query is blank or matches nothing.
    """
    query = query.strip()
    if not query:
        return []

    if "," in query:
        city_part, country_part = (part.strip() for part in query.split(",", 1))
    else:
        city_part, country_part = query, ""
    city_lower = city_part.lower()
    country_lower = country_part.lower()

    def matches_country(city: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
        if not country_lower:
            return True
        code = str(city["countrycode"]).lower()
        return country_lower == code or country_lower in _country_name(str(city["countrycode"])).lower()

    def name_matches(city: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
        # Matches either the primary name (substring) or an exact alternate
        # name/spelling (e.g. "Madras" for Chennai) - checked together, not as
        # a fallback, so a real place that happens to share an alternate
        # name's exact spelling elsewhere doesn't hide a better-known match.
        if city_lower in str(city["name"]).lower():
            return True
        return any(city_lower == str(alt).lower() for alt in city.get("alternatenames", []))

    cities = _cache.get_cities()
    candidates = [
        city for city in cities.values() if matches_country(city) and name_matches(city)
    ]

    candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (str(c["name"]).lower() != city_lower, -int(c["population"])))
    candidates = candidates[:limit]
    if not candidates:
        return []

    coords = [(float(city["latitude"]), float(city["longitude"])) for city in candidates]
    # mode=1 (single-process, in-memory) - safer than the default multiprocessing
    # mode when called from inside a running web server, and plenty fast for
    # the handful of candidates a disambiguation search ever needs.
    states = reverse_geocoder.search(coords, mode=1, verbose=False)

    return [
        PlaceMatch(
            name=str(city["name"]),
            state=str(state["admin1"]),
            country=_country_name(str(city["countrycode"])),
            latitude=float(city["latitude"]),
            longitude=float(city["longitude"]),
            timezone=str(city["timezone"]),
        )
        for city, state in zip(candidates, states)
    ]


def resolve_utc_offset(
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    local_date: date,
    local_time: time,
    timezone_name: str | None = None,
) -> float:
    """UTC offset in effect at this place on this specific date (accounts for
    historical DST rules) - derived from local IANA tzdata, not a network call.
    """
    tz_name = timezone_name or _timezone_finder.timezone_at(lat=latitude, lng=longitude)
    if tz_name is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a timezone for coordinates ({latitude}, {longitude})")
    zone = ZoneInfo(tz_name)
    aware_local = datetime.combine(local_date, local_time, tzinfo=zone)
    offset = aware_local.utcoffset()
    if offset is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve a UTC offset for timezone {tz_name!r}")
    return offset.total_seconds() / 3600

    longitude: float,

content.text: Found it — Starlette's form parser drops empty-valued fields entirely (uses `parse_qsl` without `keep_blank_values`), so an empty string and a missing field are indistinguishable to FastAPI's `Form(...)` validation. The fix is to stop relying on FastAPI's required-field check at all and let our own validation own it consistently.

"""Single-screen local web UI: one form, one rendered South Indian chart.

Runs entirely on localhost via uvicorn - the browser only ever talks to this
process on your own machine, never the internet. Place-of-birth lookup and
timezone resolution are both offline (see geocode.py) - only exact
coordinates under "Advanced" bypass them entirely.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
from pydantic import ValidationError

from vedic_astro.chart import build_kundali_chart
from vedic_astro.chart_render import south_indian_layout
from vedic_astro.geocode import resolve_utc_offset, search_places
from vedic_astro.models import BirthData, KundaliChart, NodeType

_BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

app = FastAPI(title="vedic-astro")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=_BASE_DIR / "static"), name="static")
templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=_BASE_DIR / "templates")

_AYANAMSHA_CHOICES = ["lahiri", "raman", "krishnamurti"]


def _current_local_datetime(utc_offset_hours: float) -> datetime:
    """'Now', expressed as a naive datetime in the birth place's local time -
    consistent with the naive local datetimes used throughout the dasha math."""
    now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
    return now_utc + timedelta(hours=utc_offset_hours)


def _to_24_hour_time(hour_12: int, minute: int, meridiem: str) -> time:
    if not (1 <= hour_12 <= 12):
        raise ValueError("Hour must be between 1 and 12.")
    if not (0 <= minute <= 59):
        raise ValueError("Minute must be between 0 and 59.")
    meridiem = meridiem.upper()
    if meridiem not in ("AM", "PM"):
        raise ValueError("Choose AM or PM.")
    hour_24 = (hour_12 % 12) + (12 if meridiem == "PM" else 0)
    return time(hour_24, minute)


def _empty_form_context() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "ayanamsha_choices": _AYANAMSHA_CHOICES,
        "form_values": {
            "birth_date": "",
            "birth_hour": "",
            "birth_minute": "",
            "birth_meridiem": "AM",
            "place_name": "",
            "manual_latitude": "",
            "manual_longitude": "",
            "manual_utc_offset_hours": "",
            "ayanamsha": "lahiri",
            "node_type": "mean",
        },
        "chart": None,
        "grid": None,
        "current_mahadasha": None,
        "current_antardasha": None,
        "resolved_place": None,
        "candidates": None,
        "error": None,
    }


def _render(request: Request, context: dict[str, object], status_code: int = 200) -> HTMLResponse:
    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, "index.html", context, status_code=status_code)


@app.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def show_form(request: Request) -> HTMLResponse:
    return _render(request, _empty_form_context())


@app.post("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def compute_chart(
    request: Request,
    birth_date: str = Form(...),
    birth_hour: str = Form(...),
    birth_minute: str = Form(...),
    birth_meridiem: str = Form("AM"),
    place_name: str = Form(""),
    manual_latitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_longitude: str = Form(""),
    manual_utc_offset_hours: str = Form(""),
    selected_latitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_longitude: str = Form(""),
    selected_timezone: str = Form(""),
    selected_label: str = Form(""),
    ayanamsha: str = Form("lahiri"),
    node_type: str = Form("mean"),
) -> HTMLResponse:
    context = _empty_form_context()
    context["form_values"] = {
        "birth_date": birth_date,
        "birth_hour": birth_hour,
        "birth_minute": birth_minute,
        "birth_meridiem": birth_meridiem,
        "place_name": place_name,
        "manual_latitude": manual_latitude,
        "manual_longitude": manual_longitude,
        "manual_utc_offset_hours": manual_utc_offset_hours,
        "ayanamsha": ayanamsha,
        "node_type": node_type,
    }

    try:
        parsed_date = date.fromisoformat(birth_date)
        parsed_time = _to_24_hour_time(int(birth_hour), int(birth_minute), birth_meridiem)
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = f"Invalid date or time: {exc}"
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    latitude: float | None = None
    longitude: float | None = None
    resolved_timezone: str | None = None
    resolved_place_label: str | None = None

    if selected_latitude and selected_longitude:
        # User clicked a candidate from the disambiguation list below.
        latitude = float(selected_latitude)
        longitude = float(selected_longitude)
        resolved_timezone = selected_timezone or None
        resolved_place_label = selected_label or None
    elif manual_latitude.strip() and manual_longitude.strip():
        try:
            latitude = float(manual_latitude)
            longitude = float(manual_longitude)
        except ValueError:
            context["error"] = "Latitude/longitude must be numbers."
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
    elif place_name.strip():
        matches = search_places(place_name)
        if not matches:
            context["error"] = (
                f'No place found matching "{place_name}". Try a nearby larger city, '
                "or enter exact coordinates under Advanced below."
            )
            return _render(request, context, status_code=400)
        if len(matches) > 1:
            context["candidates"] = matches
            return _render(request, context)
        latitude, longitude, resolved_timezone = (
            matches[0].latitude,
            matches[0].longitude,
            matches[0].timezone,
        )
        resolved_place_label = f"{matches[0].name}, {matches[0].state}, {matches[0].country}"
    else:
        context["error"] = "Enter a place of birth, or exact coordinates under Advanced."
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        if manual_utc_offset_hours.strip():
            utc_offset = float(manual_utc_offset_hours)
        else:
            utc_offset = resolve_utc_offset(
                latitude, longitude, parsed_date, parsed_time, resolved_timezone
            )
    except ValueError as exc:
        context["error"] = str(exc)
        return _render(request, context, status_code=400)

    try:
        birth_data = BirthData(

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name. `reverse_geocoder`
adds the state/region name (e.g. "Tamil Nadu", "Illinois") for any country,
also from a dataset bundled inside the package - this is what lets same-named
cities in different states/provinces be told apart during disambiguation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from typing import Any
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
import reverse_geocoder
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

# geonamescache's city records have no public type - treated as Any throughout
# this module rather than a stricter dict[str, object], which would force
# every field read to be re-cast before use.
_CityRecord = dict[str, Any]

# min_city_population=500 selects geonamescache's most granular bundled
# dataset (~235,000 places instead of the ~34,000-place default cutoff of
# 15,000) so small towns and villages are findable, not just major cities.
_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache(min_city_population=500)
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()

# Precomputed once at import time, not per search: with ~235,000 places and
# some carrying dozens of alternate spellings, scanning every alternate name
# of every city on every query was measured at ~1.6s/search - too slow for an
# interactive form. An index built once (a few hundred ms) makes each search
# a fast dict lookup instead of a linear scan.
_ALL_CITIES: list[_CityRecord] = list(_cache.get_cities().values())
_CITIES_WITH_LOWER_NAME: list[tuple[_CityRecord, str]] = [
    (city, str(city["name"]).lower()) for city in _ALL_CITIES
]
_ALTERNATE_NAME_INDEX: dict[str, list[_CityRecord]] = {}
for _city in _ALL_CITIES:
    for _alt in _city.get("alternatenames", []):
        _ALTERNATE_NAME_INDEX.setdefault(str(_alt).lower(), []).append(_city)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlaceMatch:
    name: str
    state: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:
    countries = _cache.get_countries()
    return str(countries.get(country_code, {}).get("name", country_code))


def search_places(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[PlaceMatch]:

"""Offline place-name -> coordinates + UTC offset resolution. No network calls.

`geonamescache` bundles a local database of ~34,000 cities (name, country,
lat/lon, IANA timezone) inside the package itself - no download, no lookup
service. `timezonefinder` similarly resolves an IANA timezone name from raw
coordinates using a bundled boundary dataset, for the case where the user
enters exact latitude/longitude instead of a place name. `reverse_geocoder`
adds the state/region name (e.g. "Tamil Nadu", "Illinois") for any country,
also from a dataset bundled inside the package - this is what lets same-named
cities in different states/provinces be told apart during disambiguation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from typing import Any
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import geonamescache
import reverse_geocoder
from timezonefinder import TimezoneFinder

# geonamescache's city records have no public type - treated as Any throughout
# this module rather than a stricter dict[str, object], which would force
# every field read to be re-cast before use.
_CityRecord = dict[str, Any]

# min_city_population=500 selects geonamescache's most granular bundled
# dataset (~235,000 places instead of the ~34,000-place default cutoff of
# 15,000) so small towns and villages are findable, not just major cities.
_cache = geonamescache.GeonamesCache(min_city_population=500)
_timezone_finder = TimezoneFinder()

# Precomputed once at import time, not per search: with ~235,000 places and
# some carrying dozens of alternate spellings, scanning every alternate name
# of every city on every query was measured at ~1.6s/search - too slow for an
# interactive form. An index built once (a few hundred ms) makes each search
# a fast dict lookup instead of a linear scan.
_ALL_CITIES: list[_CityRecord] = list(_cache.get_cities().values())
_CITIES_WITH_LOWER_NAME: list[tuple[_CityRecord, str]] = [
    (city, str(city["name"]).lower()) for city in _ALL_CITIES
]
_ALTERNATE_NAME_INDEX: dict[str, list[_CityRecord]] = {}
for _city in _ALL_CITIES:
    for _alt in _city.get("alternatenames", []):
        _ALTERNATE_NAME_INDEX.setdefault(str(_alt).lower(), []).append(_city)

    name: str
    state: str
    country: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    timezone: str


def _country_name(country_code: str) -> str:

from vedic_astro.geocode import resolve_utc_offset, search_places


def test_search_finds_chennai() -> None:
    results = search_places("Chennai")
    assert any(
        r.name == "Chennai" and r.country == "India" and r.state == "Tamil Nadu"
        for r in results
    )


def test_search_by_alternate_name_madras() -> None:
    results = search_places("Madras")
    assert any(r.name == "Chennai" for r in results)


def test_search_with_country_filter() -> None:
    results = search_places("Chennai, India")
